title: Prefixes that flip meaning
lede: A prefix is a few letters at the front that change a word's meaning. Twenty of them cover most of what you'll see.

sections.md:
## Negative prefixes
These flip a word to its opposite or remove something.

| Prefix | Meaning | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| un- | not | unfair, unlikely, unsigned |
| in-, im-, il-, ir- | not | inactive, impossible, illegal, irregular |
| dis- | not, opposite of | dishonest, disagree, disconnect |
| non- | not | nonstop, nonprofit, nonnegotiable |
| mis- | wrongly | misread, mislabel, miscalculate |
| anti- | against | antivirus, antisocial |
| counter- | against, opposite | counteroffer, counterproductive |

sections.label: in-, im-, il-, ir- are one prefix
sections.md: They're the same "not" prefix, changed to match the next sound: **im**- before b, m, p (impossible); **il**- before l (illegal); **ir**- before r (irregular); **in**- everywhere else.

## Position and time prefixes
| Prefix | Meaning | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| pre- | before | preview, prepay, precaution |
| post- | after | postpone, postwar |
| re- | again, back | rebuild, refund, reroute |
| sub- | under, below | subway, subcontract, subtotal |
| super- | above, beyond | supervisor, superhuman |
| inter- | between | interstate, interact |
| trans- | across | transport, transfer, transatlantic |
| ex- | out, former | export, ex-partner |
| co-, com-, con- | together | cooperate, combine, connect |

sections.title: Decoding with a prefix
steps: contractor = someone hired to do a job.
Put together: someone hired under another contractor.
sections.answer: A worker hired **by** the main contractor to do part of the job.

sections.label: Not every start is a prefix
sections.md: "Uncle" doesn't mean not-cle, and "interest" isn't between-est. Check that what's left is a real word or root.

options: An offer made in response, against the first

practice.why: Before r, the "not" prefix becomes ir-: irresponsible.
